title: Chicken Tikka
subtitle: Yoghurt-marinated grilled chicken cubes
excerpt: Chicken thighs marinated overnight in spiced yoghurt, then grilled in a very hot oven until charred at the edges and juicy inside. The marinade is the work; the cooking is fast.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken tikka is a Punjabi dish of spiced, grilled chicken that became a cornerstone of British Indian restaurant cooking. It is distinct from chicken tikka masala, which adds a cream and tomato sauce. The word tikka refers to small pieces or bits.

recipeTools.notes: For threading the chicken for even cooking under the grill.
To catch drips and elevate the skewers.

content.text: Chicken tikka relies almost entirely on the overnight marinade. The yoghurt tenderises the meat and carries the spices deep into the chicken, and the acid from the lemon starts to denature the proteins so the pieces cook quickly under a hot grill without drying out. Threading onto skewers and grilling at maximum heat gives the slight char at the edges that makes the dish.

items.preparation: boneless, skinless, cut into 4 cm cubes

content.text: Mix together the yoghurt, garlic, ginger, chilli powder, garam masala, ground coriander, cumin, turmeric, lemon juice, oil, and salt in a large bowl. Add the chicken and toss to coat thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for a minimum of 4 hours.

When ready to cook, heat your oven grill to maximum and position the oven shelf about 10 to 12 cm from the heat. Thread the chicken pieces onto metal skewers and rest them across a roasting tin so they sit above the tin.

Grill for 8 to 10 minutes on the first side until the chicken is charring at the edges. Turn the skewers and grill for another 8 minutes. The marinade should be charred in places and the chicken should be cooked through with no pink inside.
Rest for 3 minutes. Slide off the skewers, scatter with fresh coriander, and serve with lemon wedges, flatbreads, and a yoghurt dip or mint chutney.
